name: Elias gamma positive integer code
definition: For positive integer n let L=bitlength(n)=⌊log₂ n⌋+1 and B(n) be its canonical binary digits. G(n)=0^(L−1)⊕B(n); |G(n)|=2L−1. If k leading zeros precede the first one, read k further bits of unsigned value v (zero if empty) and recover n=2^k+v.
variables: n positive integer, L binary length, B canonical binary representation, ⊕ concatenation, k leading-zero count, v suffix value
assumptions: Exact positive integers, leading-zero unary convention (zero bits followed by a one), known bitstream end or declared number of codewords, exact binary arithmetic; n=1 encodes as 1
limitations: O(L) emitted or consumed bits and O(L) output representation; arithmetic costs depend on integer implementation. Not necessarily optimal for a specified distribution, no error correction; byte padding is not part of the code and must be separately framed
failure_conditions: Nonbinary input, missing unary terminator or truncated suffix, unexpected trailing bits under single-codeword framing
computation: Compute binary length without floating-point logarithms; prefix L−1 zero bits to canonical digits. Decode by counting zero bits, checking availability of the suffix and reconstructing the leading one plus suffix. For a sequence repeat until the exact framed end; reject truncated codeword.

source.citation: Elias (1975), Universal codeword sets and representations of the integers, IEEE Transactions on Information Theory 21(2), 194–203, DOI 10.1109/TIT.1975.1055349 (bibliographic metadata checked; original full text not reviewed). CMU 15-853 Algorithms in the Real World, Data compression continued, slide 43, https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~15853-f19/slides/compress3.pdf (uses opposite unary polarity; only the unary prefix is complemented here).

application: General integer code; no empirical benefit claimed.
required_inputs: Positive integer or framed binary code.
incompatible_methods: Treating arbitrary byte padding as codewords
mechanism_note: The unary header uniquely specifies the number of remaining binary bits, so different header lengths disagree before either can be a prefix, and equal header lengths imply equal total codeword length. Unlike a fitted Huffman tree, no symbol probability table or finite alphabet tree is needed.

name: Elias delta positive integer code
definition: For n≥1 let L=bitlength(n), B(n) canonical binary digits, and G the registered leading-zero gamma code. D(n)=G(L)⊕B(n)[1:L]; |D(n)|=L+2⌊log₂ L⌋. Decode L from G, then read L−1 suffix bits of unsigned value v and recover n=2^(L−1)+v.
variables: n positive integer, L binary length, G gamma code, B canonical binary digits, ⊕ concatenation, v suffix value; slice indices zero-based, end exclusive
assumptions: Exact positive integers, shared leading-zero gamma convention, known bitstream end or declared codeword count, no implicit padding; n=1 encodes as 1
limitations: O(L+log L) emitted or consumed bits; integer arithmetic and storage depend on representation. Delta may be longer than gamma for small values; no universal finite-stream compression guarantee or error correction
failure_conditions: Malformed or truncated gamma header or truncated binary suffix; unexpected trailing bits under single-codeword framing
Decoded length exceeds remaining bits or declared resource bound
computation: Obtain exact bit length L, gamma encode L and append all but the leading binary one of n. Parse gamma header, validate decoded length against available input and resource limits before allocating, then reconstruct n with the implicit leading one.

source.citation: Elias (1975), Universal codeword sets and representations of the integers, IEEE Transactions on Information Theory 21(2), 194–203, DOI 10.1109/TIT.1975.1055349 (bibliographic metadata checked; original full text not reviewed). Mansouri (2022), University of Southern Maine, Introduction to Information Retrieval, Session 5, slide 35, https://cs.usm.maine.edu/~behrooz.mansouri/courses/Slides_IR_22/Introduction%20to%20Information%20Retrieval%20--%20Session%205%20-%20Indexing%20%26%20Ranking.pdf (gamma-coded length followed by binary remainder; here leading-zero gamma convention).

application: General integer code; no empirical benefit claimed.
required_inputs: Positive integer or framed binary code.
incompatible_methods: Allocating from untrusted decoded length without bounds
mechanism_note: Gamma's unary length header is replaced by a gamma code for L, while the binary remainder is unchanged. Prefix-freeness follows from gamma header prefix-freeness and the fixed remaining length once L is decoded. This nested header is a material variant of gamma rather than an independent algorithm count.
